title: TAGR: Task-Adaptive Geo-Semantic Retrieval across Heterogeneous Urban Delivery Tasks
abstract: arXiv:2610.28638v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: As urban residents demand higher-quality instant delivery services, demand forecasting, estimated time of arrival prediction, and next-stop prediction have become critical tasks in urban delivery systems. However, the three tasks rely on historical evidence with substantially different structures and granularities. Meanwhile, their prediction targets differ in output form, making it difficult to integrate retrieved evidence through a single fusion mechanism without causing mismatch or negative transfer. These issues can increase prediction errors and subsequently lead to imbalanced resource allocation, where some regions experience unmet demand. In contrast, others suffer from underutilization, ultimately degrading overall efficiency and service quality. translated_title: TAGR：面向异构城市配送任务的任务自适应地理语义检索
translated_abstract: 随着城市居民对高质量即时配送服务需求的不断提升，需求预测、预计到达时间（ETA）预测和下一站预测已成为城市配送系统中的关键任务。然而，这三项任务所依赖的历史证据在结构和粒度上存在显著差异。同时，它们的预测目标在输出形式上也各不相同，这使得难以通过单一的融合机制来整合检索到的证据，否则会造成匹配不当或负迁移。这些问题会增加预测误差，进而导致资源配置失衡——部分地区的需求得不到满足，而另一些地区则出现资源利用率不足的情况，最终降低整体效率和服务质量。为应对这些挑战，我们提出了TAGR，一个面向异构城市配送任务的任务自适应地理语义检索框架。TAGR构建了一个基于大语言模型（LLM）的地理语义共享……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 提出TAGR框架，通过任务自适应的地理语义检索机制，为城市配送中需求预测、ETA预测和下一站预测三类异构任务检索结构与粒度各异的历史证据，解决单一融合机制导致的匹配不当与负迁移问题，提升预测精度与资源分配效率。
en_tdlr: TAGR is a task-adaptive geo-semantic retrieval framework that retrieves structurally and granularly tailored historical evidence for heterogeneous urban delivery tasks—demand forecasting, ETA prediction, and next-stop prediction—overcoming mismatch and negative transfer from single fusion mechanisms.
